blindSummary: No documented sub-national signal for this state/province: the country-level review lists this state/province among the units where no region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding could be located, and all three attached sources are national in scope. What binds this state/province is the national frame: a congressional bill package (two bills, committee-approved February 2025) would bar trans people from public sanitary facilities of the opposite sex at birth, and national data record 54 killings and 170 rights-violation cases of LGBTI people between 2020 and 2023 with trans women most affected and hate crimes rising - no region-specific evidence in either direction.
blindSourceSummaries: A national news outlet's report (20 Feb 2025): the congressional committee on women and family unanimously approved the report backing two bills, which bar trans people from public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite their birth sex - with exceptions for custody, medical care and accompanying children under 12, elderly or disabled people - and require unambiguous facility signage; the opinion still needs full-chamber approval. A quoted LGBTI activist calls the measure discriminatory.

A private university's human-rights institute bulletin: academic critique of the congressional bathroom ban - argues the law implicitly brands trans people as a sexual risk to minors in facilities, citing a lawmaker's ridicule of trans bathroom use; part of the institute's coverage of legalised discrimination (including rulings by the national consumer-protection agency).

An LGBTI news outlet's report (22 Jul 2024) on a private university research centre's annual report: 54 killings of LGBTI people and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023, with trans women the most affected group and hate crimes rising; includes testimony on the February 2023 murder of a trans woman kidnapped from the capital city centre and shot dead by a criminal gang in a district of the capital.
